fixture.reason: The provider-side proof target did not change, so M56 and P_I5 remain valid for the sealed K5 attempt domain. weak_rule_falsified.rule: If the provider terminal proof and execution domain are unchanged, a previously valid repository fence/CAS result may be replayed after a claim-epoch change.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: A claim-epoch change can transfer or invalidate repository-side authority without changing the provider attempt domain. Reusing stale F7 would therefore bypass current ownership/conflict checks even though P_I5 is still sound. Provider-proof stability does not imply repository-fence freshness.

fixture.minimum_safe_rule: Across an interrupted finalize with unchanged sealed provider domain, retain provider evidence only for the exact unchanged domain, but reacquire current repository claim authority and require fresh CAS plus exact readback before finalization. Historical fence/CAS evidence is provenance only and never substitutes for the current claim epoch.

observations: Provider execution-domain closure and repository claim freshness are orthogonal safety dimensions.
An interruption may leave provider terminal evidence reusable while invalidating only repository-side ownership/fence evidence.
A stale repository CAS result cannot be promoted to current authority merely because the external no-effect proof remains valid.
inference: Within this exact deterministic fixture, the safe recovery rule is asymmetric: retain domain-scoped provider terminal evidence when the sealed execution domain is unchanged, but reacquire repository claim freshness after any claim-epoch transition and require fresh CAS/readback. This narrows the unresolved concurrency rule without claiming a concrete provider implementation.
